answer: Group agents that share deposit sources, routing, or near-copy answers into one cluster, then settle that cluster with a square-root payout instead of paying every account in full. A nebula of cloned identities therefore collapses toward a single reward. To earn N times more, an attacker must fund and operate about N squared uncorrelated agents, buying separate capital and hardware each time, a cost that stacks as heavily as shale. Only those separated identities can collect at the settlement wharf, so cheap mass registration stops paying.
